stories.headline: China prohibits SoftBank's $5.4B takeover of ABB's robotics business in China; deal in doubt

key_facts.fact: ABB said on Nov 5 that SoftBank informed it that China's Office of the Working Mechanism for Foreign Investment Security Review prohibited the acquisition of the ABB Robotics business in China; ABB says the two are in close dialogue and working constructively on the transaction, signed in October 2025 at a $5.375B enterprise value.
key_facts.excerpt: ABB confirms that it has been informed by SoftBank that the Office of the Working Mechanism for Foreign Investment Security Review in China has prohibited the acquisition of the ABB Robotics business in China. ABB and SoftBank are in close dialogue and are working constructively on the transaction.

key_facts.fact: The FT first reported the prohibition on Nov 5, saying SoftBank expected the deal to go through until it was told last week that China's National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC) had prohibited it; SoftBank declined to comment and the NDRC did not immediately respond.
key_facts.excerpt: The prohibition was first reported by the Financial Times on Nov 5. SoftBank had expected the deal to go through until it was told last week that China's National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC) had prohibited the acquisition, the report said.

key_facts.fact: Per the FT, the NDRC was concerned that robotics data could be transferred overseas and used to train AI models, including those of OpenAI, in which SoftBank is a major investor.
key_facts.excerpt: The NDRC was concerned about robotics data being transferred overseas, where it could be used to train AI models, including those developed by OpenAI, in which SoftBank is a major investor, the FT report added.

key_facts.fact: China is ABB's largest robotics market, and more than 90% of robots for Chinese customers are built locally, including at a $150M Shanghai factory operating since 2022.
key_facts.excerpt: China is the largest market for ABB's robotics division. More than 90% of the robots destined for Chinese customers are manufactured locally. ABB has been operating a robot factory in Shanghai since 2022, built at a cost of $150 million.

key_facts.fact: It is the second major deal China has blocked this year, after Meta was ordered to unwind its $2B-plus acquisition of AI startup Manus.
key_facts.excerpt: The case marks the second major deal blocked by China this year after Meta Platforms was ordered to unwind its US$2 billion-plus acquisition of artificial intelligence start-up Manus.

key_facts.fact: The FT says a spin-off of parts of the business to Chinese owners had been considered and that SoftBank is assessing whether a fresh attempt is possible; the European Commission had already approved the takeover.
key_facts.excerpt: a spin-off of parts of the business to Chinese owners had also been considered. The report stated that the decision came as a surprise to SoftBank... It is now assessing whether a fresh attempt is possible... The European Commission had already approved the takeover.

key_facts.fact: ABB expected about $5.3B in net proceeds from the sale and recently announced a $5.5B purchase of British automation specialist Rotork.
key_facts.excerpt: ABB had previously anticipated net proceeds of around $5.3 billion... ABB recently announced the purchase of the British automation specialist Rotork for $5.5 billion.

key_facts.fact: China represents around 30% of ABB's robot-related business, and ABB shares were down 1.1% in morning trading after the block became public.
key_facts.excerpt: ABB shares were down 1.1% in morning trading after the blocked takeover was made public... China is ABB's biggest robotics market, representing around 30% of its robot-related business.

stories.headline: Bloomberg: Micron halts $4.5B Taiwan memory plant over labor dispute amid AI memory shortage

key_facts.fact: Micron has all but halted construction of its plant in Taoyuan, Taiwan, over a protracted labor dispute and has told Taiwanese officials and a supplier, according to people cited by Bloomberg.
key_facts.excerpt: The US company has all but halted construction of a plant in the northern Taiwanese city of Taoyuan... Micron has informed Taiwanese officials and a supplier about its plans to suspend construction in the city, the people said.

key_facts.fact: The site, Fab 11E, had a budget of $3B to $4.5B including ASML equipment, was due online in 2028 and was planned to make high-bandwidth memory (HBM) and DRAM.
key_facts.excerpt: Micron had budgeted US$3 billion to US$4.5 billion towards the Taoyuan complex, which included purchases of ASML gear... Dubbed Fab 11E, it was previously scheduled to come online in 2028.

key_facts.fact: Micron did not address the Taoyuan complex directly, saying operations continue as normal; the Taoyuan government says it has not been notified of a suspension.
key_facts.excerpt: "Taiwan plays an important role in Micron's global footprint, and our operations today continue as normal," Micron said in a statement, without addressing questions about the Taoyuan complex... The Taoyuan government said it hasn't been notified of a suspension.

key_facts.fact: The Taoyuan union, fewer than 3,000 of Micron's 15,000 Taiwan staff, demands that 15% of operating profit go to employees, matching Samsung and SK Hynix, and is recruiting from the larger Taichung union to annul the pact that union signed in October.
key_facts.excerpt: The Taoyuan group has demanded Micron distribute 15% of its operating profit to global employees, because Samsung and SK Hynix have adopted similar measures... The union is now trying to form a bigger group by recruiting members from the Taichung body -- to help try and annul the existing pact.

key_facts.fact: Taiwan's economic ministry says the October deal would lift junior engineers' annual packages to about NT$4M ($121,450) on average and senior engineers' to NT$6M.
key_facts.excerpt: the agreement would lift junior engineers' annual packages by more than two-fold to NT$4 million (US$121,450...), on average. Senior engineers would get a three-fold bump to NT$6 million.

key_facts.fact: Taiwan produces three-fifths of Micron's conventional chips, and Micron has invested close to $50B there over three decades.
key_facts.excerpt: an island that produces three-fifths of the US firm's conventional chips... Micron -- which has invested close to US$50 billion... in Taiwan over three decades

key_facts.fact: Micron and the Taoyuan union are set to meet again on Nov 6, after a one-day strike last month.
key_facts.excerpt: the Taoyuan union is still holding out for better terms, with the two parties set to meet again on November 6. It even launched a one-day strike last month

stories.headline: Agility closes SPAC, lists on Nasdaq as first US pure-play humanoid firm; $174K H1 revenue

key_facts.fact: Agility closed its merger with Churchill Capital Corp XI on Nov 4, with stock and warrants set to trade on Nasdaq from Nov 5 as AGLT and AGLTW; it bills itself as the only US-listed pure-play humanoid company with active commercial deployments.
key_facts.excerpt: today announced the completion of its previously announced business combination with Churchill Capital Corp XI... expected to begin trading on Nasdaq on November 5, 2026, under the ticker symbols "AGLT" and "AGLTW"... the only U.S. publicly listed pure-play humanoid robotics company with proven, active commercial deployments

key_facts.fact: The deal and related financings raised about $465M gross, including a PIPE (private investment in public equity) led by Foxconn and $100M of equity received before closing.
key_facts.excerpt: The business combination and related financings raised approximately $465 million in gross capital before transaction expenses, including proceeds from a private investment in public equity (PIPE) led by Foxconn and $100 million of equity funding received prior to closing.

key_facts.fact: SPAC shareholder redemptions cut the capital raised in the deal to the final $465M.
key_facts.excerpt: With SPAC shareholder redemptions the capital raised in the deal drops to $465M.

key_facts.fact: Agility earned just $174,000 in revenue in the first half of 2026, mostly from related parties, and lost $362M in the same period.
key_facts.excerpt: the robot is actually doing real work, and earning money -- albeit just $174,000 in the first six months of 2026, and mostly from related parties. The company lost $362 million in the same time period

key_facts.fact: TechCrunch reports $300M in planned Digit 5 contracts from 30 customers; the CEO would not name them or say whether they are investors, and Digit 5 must hit undisclosed performance targets to close the deals.
key_facts.excerpt: Agility has $300 million in planned contracts from 30 customers for its new generation of robot, Digit 5... could not yet reveal who the customers or say if they are investors. To close the deals, Johnson said that Digit 5 will have to hit undisclosed targets along several metrics

key_facts.fact: Its filing estimates a subscription at $25,000 upfront per robot plus $8,500 a month, or $200,000 to buy plus $20,000 for deployment and $36,000 a year; Digit 5's bill of materials starts at $150,000, targeted to fall to $30,000 at 10,000 robots a year.
key_facts.excerpt: customers would pay a one-time cost of about $25,000 per robot for delivery and deployment... along with a recurring monthly fee of $8,500... purchase the robot's hardware outright for a one-time payment of $200,000... estimated each Digit v5 humanoid robot as initially costing Agility $150,000... eventually $30,000 per robot if the company can produce 10,000 robots per year.

key_facts.fact: Digit 5 prototypes have not been shown publicly; the CEO says they will be demonstrated at CES 2027 and be widely available at the end of 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: The company has yet to show off the prototypes of Digit 5, but Johnson said they will be demonstrated at CES 2027 and widely available at the end of that year.

stories.headline: FT: Microsoft declined option to more than double Nscale Texas deal, a blow before $35B IPO

key_facts.fact: The FT reported on Nov 5 that Microsoft rejected an option to more than double its contract to rent computing power at Nscale's Ward County, Texas site, a potential deal worth tens of billions of dollars.
key_facts.excerpt: Microsoft rejected an option that would have more than doubled the size of its existing contract to rent computing power at the Ward County site, a potential deal worth tens of billions of dollars, the report said citing three people familiar with the matter.

key_facts.fact: A source told Reuters the decision was made several months ago, before Nscale filed for its IPO in September, that the existing Texas contract is unaffected and that Nscale's total contract value of about $103B does not change.
key_facts.excerpt: Microsoft's decision to not expand the contract was made several months ago, before Nscale filed for its IPO in September, and added that its existing Texas contract with Microsoft was not affected... no impact on Nscale's total contract value of about $103 billion

key_facts.fact: The option was announced as a 700 MW second phase in October 2025; Nscale told the FT this week it was closer to 500 MW.
key_facts.excerpt: In October 2025, Nscale announced a deal to lease to Microsoft about 240 megawatts... with an option on a second phase of 700 megawatts. Nscale told the FT this week the option was closer to 500 megawatts

key_facts.fact: Nscale, preparing a roughly $35B IPO, lost $1B on revenue of $141M in the first half of 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: as it prepares a roughly $35 billion IPO... Nscale made a net loss of $1 billion on revenue of $141 million in the first half of 2026.

key_facts.fact: This follows Microsoft pulling out in October of a deal to anchor Nscale's Loughton, Essex site after grid delays pushed its power supply into the 2030s.
key_facts.excerpt: In October, Microsoft pulled out of a deal to anchor Nscale's site in Loughton, Essex, billed as the UK's largest AI data centre. Grid delays had pushed its power supply into the 2030s.

key_facts.fact: Nscale's flagship West Virginia site, central to its $45B computing deal with Anthropic, faces construction delays and local opposition; Nscale is in talks with Anthropic to lease a second 460 MW data center there.
key_facts.excerpt: Nscale's flagship West Virginia site, central to its $45 billion computing deal with Anthropic, has also faced construction delays and local opposition... in talks with Anthropic to expand its deal to lease a second 460-megawatt data center there.

stories.headline: OpenAI vows no NDAs with officials and to pay full power costs after midterm data center rout

key_facts.fact: OpenAI published a National Community Compact and a Compute Campus Policy Blueprint on Nov 5; it pledges to pay the full cost of its electricity and serving infrastructure, with financial assurances protecting other customers if a project is delayed, reduced or canceled.
key_facts.excerpt: We'll pay the full cost of the electricity we use and the infrastructure needed to serve us. Before major spending begins, we'll provide financial assurances so other customers are protected if a project is delayed, reduced, or canceled.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI says it will not use NDAs with public officials, except narrow protections for security information, trade secrets or competitively sensitive information, and will publish site-level water and electricity use, construction plans and independent noise studies.
key_facts.excerpt: we will not use non-disclosure agreements (NDAs) with public officials, allowing only narrow protections covering legitimate security information, trade secrets, or proprietary or competitively sensitive information.

key_facts.fact: The commitments apply only to future campuses that OpenAI owns and operates.
key_facts.excerpt: Moving forward, every campus owned and operated by OpenAI will have its own locally tailored Community Compact... At future sites owned and operated by OpenAI, we will share clear, timely information about compute campus development

key_facts.fact: OpenAI's agreement with Georgia Power for its Effingham County campus lets the utility cut up to 1,000 MW delivered to it during periods of high demand.
key_facts.excerpt: At our planned Effingham County campus, for example, our agreement with Georgia Power allows the utility to reduce the power it delivers to us by up to 1,000 megawatts during periods of high demand.

key_facts.fact: OpenAI's Lehane said the commitments build on earlier initiatives and the blueprint had been in the works since August; CNBC notes OpenAI has repeatedly pledged to protect ratepayers this year.
key_facts.excerpt: OpenAI has repeatedly pledged to protect ratepayers and invest in local communities this year, and Lehane said the company's latest commitments build on many of its previous initiatives. He said the policy blueprint has been in the works since August

key_facts.fact: The WSJ reports that by Wednesday morning senior OpenAI leaders were discussing whether the results meant resetting expectations for next year's data center capacity, after executives at Jensen Huang's election-night event voiced concern.
key_facts.excerpt: WSJ: By Wednesday morning, senior leaders at OpenAI were discussing whether the results meant the company would have to reset expectations regarding its data center capacity next year, according to a person familiar with the conversation.

key_facts.fact: Axios counts restrictive measures across 10 states going 43-1 at the ballot box, with analysts saying about 60% of planned 2028 US capacity faces a risk of delay.
key_facts.excerpt: restrictive measures across 10 states going 43-1 at the ballot box... Analysts say about 60% of planned 2028 capacity across the U.S. faces a risk of delay.

stories.headline: Qualcomm drops about 9% premarket as handset chip sales fall 26% in memory crunch

key_facts.fact: Qualcomm's fiscal Q4 handset revenue fell 26% to $5.14B, missing the $5.25B estimate, and pulled chip segment revenue down 8% to $9.02B.
key_facts.excerpt: Revenue from Qualcomm's handset unit, which makes chips for smartphones, fell 26 per cent to $5.14 billion in the fourth quarter, dragging the chip segment's revenue down 8 per cent to $9.02 billion. Analysts polled by Visible Alpha expected handset revenue of $5.25 billion.

key_facts.fact: Adjusted revenue of $10.44B fell 7% but beat the $10.12B estimate; adjusted EPS was $2.17 versus $2.16 expected; gross margin of 52.4% missed the 53.2% estimate.
key_facts.excerpt: Adjusted revenue reached $10.44 billion, exceeding expectations of $10.12 billion but declining 7% from $11.27 billion a year earlier... Qualcomm reported a fourth-quarter gross margin of 52.4%, compared with analysts' expectations of 53.2%.

key_facts.fact: Shares dropped about 9% premarket on Nov 5, on track to erase about $17.5B of market value if losses held.
key_facts.excerpt: Qualcomm shares dropped about 9% in premarket trading on Thursday... If premarket losses hold, Qualcomm is on track to shed about $17.5 billion in market value.

key_facts.fact: For fiscal Q1 it guided revenue to $10.4B-$11.2B, a midpoint above consensus, but EPS to $2.15-$2.35, with a midpoint of $2.25 below the $2.32 expected; pricing moves against higher input costs only reach full benefit in the second half of fiscal 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: Qualcomm projected revenue between $10.4 billion and $11.2 billion... adjusted earnings forecast of $2.15 to $2.35 per share had a midpoint of $2.25, below analysts' expectations of $2.32... the full financial benefit is not expected until the second half of fiscal 2027.

key_facts.fact: CEO Cristiano Amon said the Q1 forecast includes no further Apple sales and that Android handset sales have bottomed out and are ticking up.
key_facts.excerpt: Amon said the first-quarter fiscal 2027 forecast given on Wednesday includes no further sales from Apple... Qualcomm CEO Cristiano Amon said sales of Android handsets had bottomed out and were ticking upward again.

key_facts.fact: Global smartphone shipments fell 20% in the September quarter to a 14-year low, per Counterpoint, as memory costs drove up device prices.
key_facts.excerpt: Global smartphone shipments fell 20 per cent in the September quarter to a 14-year low, according to Counterpoint Research, as surging memory chip costs drove up device prices

key_facts.fact: Automotive revenue rose 89% to $1.99B and IoT 4% to $1.89B; Amon says fiscal 2027 marks the start of a non-handset revenue inflection, including the data center ramp.
key_facts.excerpt: Qualcomm's automotive business reported revenue of $1.99 billion, an increase of 89% year over year... "Fiscal 2027 marks the start of our non-handset revenue inflection, including the ramp of our Data Center business," Amon said.

stories.headline: Arm beats with $1.44B quarter and backs $2B AGI CPU goal, but thin guide sinks shares

key_facts.fact: Arm's fiscal Q2 revenue rose 27% to $1.44B, a record for a second quarter and above the $1.38B estimate; adjusted EPS of 52 cents beat the 47 cents expected.
key_facts.excerpt: The company's second-quarter revenue of $1.44 billion beat analysts' average estimate of $1.38 billion... Arm's adjusted profit of 52 cents per share surpassed estimates of 47 cents per share.

key_facts.fact: Licensing revenue rose 50% to $773M against a $625.1M estimate, while royalties rose only 8% to $670M, below the $720.8M estimate.
key_facts.excerpt: Revenue from royalties... rose 8% to $670 million for the second quarter, compared with estimates of $720.8 million. Licensing revenue... was $773 million, compared with estimates of $625.1 million.

key_facts.fact: Arm guided fiscal Q3 revenue to $1.54B, plus or minus $50M, against a $1.53B consensus, and shares fell more than 3% premarket on Nov 5.
key_facts.excerpt: U.S.-listed shares of the British chip designer fell more than 3% in premarket trading Thursday... For its fiscal Q3 2027, ARM sees adjusted profit per share of 56 cents plus/minus 4 cents on revenue of $1.54 billion plus/minus $50 million. The consensus estimates had been for a profit of 55 cents per share on revenue of $1.53 billion.

key_facts.fact: Arm says its confidence in up to $2B of revenue from its own chip, the AGI CPU, across fiscal 2027 and 2028 has increased, with purchase orders from multiple customers through calendar 2027 and first commercial deliveries on track for fiscal Q4.
key_facts.excerpt: Arm's confidence in achieving up to $2 billion in Arm AGI CPU revenue over FYE27 and FYE28 has increased over the past 90 days... Purchase orders for Arm AGI CPU have been secured from multiple customers extending through calendar 2027, and the first commercial deliveries are on track for Q4 FYE27.

key_facts.fact: Data center royalties doubled year over year, and Arm says its server share at top hyperscalers exceeded 50% in 2025 and will pass 60% by the end of 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Arm-based server market share at the top hyperscalers more than tripled -- from 15% in calendar 2024 to more than 50% in calendar 2025... Arm expects that share to exceed 60% by the end of calendar 2026

key_facts.fact: Partners shipped more than 10 billion Arm-based chips in a quarter for the first time, up 1.5 billion from a year earlier.
key_facts.excerpt: For the first time, Arm's partners reported more than 10 billion Arm-based chips shipped during the quarter -- an increase of 1.5 billion chips year over year

key_facts.fact: Analysts surveyed by Bloomberg averaged $1.53B for the quarter, though some projections neared $1.7B.
key_facts.excerpt: Analysts surveyed by Bloomberg had expected $1.53 billion on average, although some projections neared $1.7 billion.
